newsitem.title: ESTONIA: ESTONIAN SHARES IN NEW RECORDS, FEW SELLERS SEEN.
newsitem.headline: ESTONIAN SHARES IN NEW RECORDS, FEW SELLERS SEEN.

text.p: Blue chip stock prices captured more records on Thursday as the bourse index soared through the 400 points level with dealers saying there was no end in sight.
Total trade on the main list was 193.1 million kroons as the Talse index rose 3.90 percent to leap over the 400 level for a close of 413.20.
"The bourse is still driven by good results news and low liquidity," said one analyst.
Hoiupank reached 261 kroons after rising 10 kroons on trade worth a huge 83.2 million kroons.
"There are not many sellers around and so the price has nowhere to go but up," one dealer said.
Hoiupank revised its profit forecast on Wednesday taking it to 297.5 million kroons from 140 million kroons to give more support to the stock's price levels.
"While there is such good news about, there is no reason for stock prices to fall, but a correction is of course possible," another trader said.
Hansapank matched Hoiupank to gain 6.90 kroons and closed at 231.90 kroons after turning over 38.8 million kroons.
Dealers said say investors believe that the price levels of Hoiu and Hansa should be similar and this has kept Hansa up with Hoiu's gains.
Forekspank was 5.50 kroons lower as reports about the bank's frozen bank account in St Petersburg worked through the market.
The St Petersburg tax police are said to have ordered the freezing of several Estonian correspondent accounts for what the tax police said was failure to comply with Russian tax regulations.
Tallinna Pank was also affected by the reports to be lower by one kroon to close on 65 kroons.
On the free market, total trade was only 5.2 million kroons with privatisation securities the most active stock.
The securities turned over 2.9 million kroons to close up on Wednesday at 0.415 vs 0.401 kroons.
